Deposit. Hold encrypted notes. Withdraw.

A deposit moves assets from a public wallet into the protocol pool. The browser creates encrypted notes and a zero-knowledge proof. A withdrawal spends private notes through the protocol relayer and pays a public recipient wallet.

Private balances come from locally decrypting encrypted notes and checking whether they remain unspent. The first scan may download substantial historical data. A dash means unread, not zero.

Your unlock signature is sensitive.

The SDK derives private-note keys from the exact wallet signature for “Privacy Money account sign in”. Hushmark verifies two matching signatures and stores a recovery fingerprint. Never share the signature. Another site requesting the same message could obtain access to the same private notes.

Use the same Phantom or Solflare software wallet for recovery. The SDK does not support hardware wallets. Signatures and decryption keys remain in memory; encrypted-note caches and scan offsets are stored in this tab’s session storage, scoped to the connected account. A signature fingerprint is stored locally to detect recovery changes.

Approve the exact outcome.

Deposit fees are shown in the wallet. Withdrawals deduct the configured protocol fee from the entered amount. Hushmark compares the relay payload with the reviewed recipient, mint, amount and fee. Partial withdrawals are rejected if the two largest available notes cannot fund the approved amount.

A withdrawal can submit using the already unlocked note keys without another wallet popup. Clicking Confirm authorizes that withdrawal. A relayer response is not finality: inspect the signature and use Check finality. If submission is uncertain, check the balance and transaction before retrying.

Unlinkability is not invisibility.

The funding address and deposit amount are public. The recipient and withdrawal amount are public. Protocol proofs aim to conceal which deposit funded which withdrawal. The available anonymity set, matching amounts, timing, address reuse and other activity can weaken that protection.

The RPC and Privacy Cash relayer can observe network metadata. The SDK also asks the relayer for indices of matching encrypted notes, exposing those queried note identifiers to that service. Availability, fee policy and protocol behavior depend on these third-party services. There is no claim of affiliation with Privacy Cash or Zcash, perfect anonymity, or a security audit of Hushmark.

The interface uses the Privacy Cash SDK and proving assets to generate proofs locally for SOL and USDC.

Your activity, saved locally.

Hushmark records new deposit and withdrawal attempts initiated in this browser. The latest 100 records are encrypted in local storage with AES-GCM, using a separate key derived from your verified unlock signature. Unlocking the same wallet on the same browser and site lets you read them again. Locking discards the history key and removes the decrypted list from the page. No additional signature is requested for this feature.

The records include the asset, amount, protocol fee, time, status and transaction signature when available. Recipient addresses are not saved. Withdrawal records also keep a hash of the approved proof so finality checks can verify the returned transaction after a reload. A submitted signature, a confirmed transaction and a finalized transaction are different states. An interrupted request or missing transaction must not be treated as a safe invitation to retry.

This is a local activity log, not your complete onchain history or a backup of your funds. It does not scan earlier transactions automatically. Use an encrypted history backup to transfer saved records from another browser or domain with the same wallet. Clearing site data or local history deletes the log; it does not withdraw funds or erase public transactions. Your original software wallet is still needed to recover private notes through the protocol.

No analytics backend receives this journal, and status checks are not run automatically when history is opened. Refresh status queries your configured Solana RPC. Opening Explorer visits a third-party service. Browser storage exposes the wallet address used to scope the encrypted journal. Encryption protects stored content while locked; it cannot protect against a compromised browser or site while unlocked. Storage failure leaves wallet operations available, but the local history can be incomplete.

Back up your activity history.

While unlocked, choose Download backup to save an encrypted JSON file. Restore it with the same software wallet on another browser or domain. Hushmark validates and merges the file locally, keeps existing records and retains the latest 100. Conflicting or corrupted files are rejected without replacing your history. New restored records are marked unverified until you check their network status. Backup files contain a public wallet address and encrypted history; no seed phrase, unlock signature or private-note spending key is exported.

This is a backup of activity records only. It does not recover funds, replace your original wallet or restore private notes. Keep the original software wallet for protocol recovery. No history file is uploaded to a backend.

Sessions expire when idle.

Auto-lock defaults to five minutes and can be changed to fifteen or thirty. It clears unlocked history, review details and in-memory keys when you stop interacting. Background tabs are checked again on return and before guarded actions. Auto-lock can interrupt proof generation or a pending wallet prompt. A transaction already sent may still complete; the last saved uncertain status stays available after unlocking, so check it before retrying.

Request a payment by link or QR.

Create a SOL or USDC request with a recipient, net amount and expiry. Links use the website's own wallet page and keep details in a URL fragment. The address and amount are readable by anyone who has the link. The request is not signed identity verification, a stealth address, a private invoice or proof of payment.

The payer unlocks the wallet, explicitly chooses Use this request, then reviews the amount debited, current protocol fee and exact recipient amount. Hushmark calculates the gross withdrawal needed for that amount. Editing the payment fields detaches the shared request; expired requests cannot authorize a new payment. Opening a link never submits a transaction, and no automatic Paid status is claimed.

Read current service availability.

Check services makes read-only requests to the configured RPC and Privacy Cash's fee endpoint. It verifies Solana mainnet, a finalized slot, the executable privacy program and valid fee configuration. Results include the check time and can become stale. An available endpoint is not an audit, deposit guarantee, or verification that the relayer can complete a withdrawal. Changing RPC clears old results. No automatic provider switching or transaction retry occurs.

Token status.

HUSHM is the Hushmark project token on Solana. The private pool supports SOL and USDC. Holding or transferring HUSHM does not make a transaction private.
